title: Is tourism destroying the places we love?
situation: A travel magazine for young people is holding a writing competition on the topic "Is tourism destroying the places we love?" The best articles will be published on the magazine's website. Write an article for the competition.
situationHu: Egy ifjúsági utazási magazin cikkíró pályázatot hirdetett arról, hogy a turizmus tönkreteszi-e a kedvelt helyeinket.

points.text: describe a popular place you know that is affected by large numbers of tourists
discuss the benefits that tourism brings to local people
explain the problems that too many tourists can cause
suggest how travellers could visit places more responsibly

usefulPhrases.en: Tourism is a major source of income for …
usefulPhrases.hu: A turizmus jelentős bevételi forrás … számára.

usefulPhrases.en: Local residents are being forced out of the city centre.
usefulPhrases.hu: A helyi lakosokat kiszorítják a belvárosból.

usefulPhrases.en: Not only does tourism …, but it also …
It is up to us as travellers to …

checklistExtra: Adtam a cikknek címet, és a bevezetőben felkeltettem az olvasó érdeklődését?

modelAnswer.text:
Loving Places to Death?

Every weekend, thousands of tourists pour into the old Jewish Quarter of Budapest. Its narrow streets are full of ruin bars, food stalls and souvenir shops, and on Saturday nights it is almost impossible to walk along the pavement.

There is no doubt that tourism brings real benefits. It is a major source of income for the city, and many local people work in hotels, restaurants and shops that would not exist without visitors. Tourist money has also helped to restore old buildings that were falling apart twenty years ago.

However, not only does mass tourism make the area overcrowded, but it also changes the lives of the people who live there. Since so many flats are now rented out to tourists, rents and house prices have risen sharply, and local residents are being forced out of the city centre. Those who stay often complain about noise late at night and litter in the streets.

So what can we do? It is up to us as travellers to make a difference. We could travel off-season and stay in hotels instead of holiday flats. It is also worth exploring less famous neighbourhoods and supporting local businesses rather than international chains. Above all, we should remember that every tourist hotspot is somebody's home.

Tourism does not have to destroy the places we love – as long as we travel with respect.

notes: Feladat teljesítése: a cikk egy valós, konkrét helyet mutat be (a budapesti zsidónegyed), két előnyt, több problémát (lakásárak, kiszorulás, zaj, szemét) és három gyakorlati javaslatot ad – mind a négy szempont érdemben kifejtett.

Szövegalkotás: pályázati cikkhez illő figyelemfelkeltő cím és élénk nyitókép, kiegyensúlyozott érvelés (There is no doubt that … / However, …), retorikai kérdés az átvezetésnél (So what can we do?) és erős zárómondat.

Nyelvhelyesség: változatos B2-es szerkezetek – inverzió (not only does mass tourism make …, but it also …), present perfect passive és present continuous passive (are being forced out), feltételes would.
Szókincs: érdemes megtanulni: a major source of income, mass tourism, travel off-season, every tourist hotspot is somebody's home.
